title: Two Runs Out of Nenana
concept: In January 1925 diphtheria threatened Nome; antitoxin came by train to Nenana, the railroad's closest point, and 20 mushers ran it 674 miles by dog team, because nobody knew how a small engine would take 40 below. On August 19th UAF's drone center flew a Windracers ULTRA out of Nenana, piloted remotely, with human blood samples for the International Testing Agency; each volunteer gave two samples so one flew and one stayed. It flew 8 hours 47 minutes and 1,000 km, about 621 miles, nearly the length of the serum trail, in a loop that landed where it started. UAF has flown small drones at 40 below, and director Cathy Cahill says the flight proves the blood could survive. The test: no lab results have been published, so the film claims the trip, not the result. The state says 82 percent of communities are off the road; federal rules regulate against flying beyond the operator's line of sight; UAF plans detect-and-avoid radar, which Cahill calls a key step, and has partnered with Ryan Air and Tanana Chiefs Conference to develop or test medical delivery. Drawn as two faced sample tubes, FLEW and STAYED, a plain cargo drone with no face, a dashed phosphor radar that stays PLANNED, and a scarlet ribbon that is a loop until it is laid along the 1925 paw trail on a map on the river ice, about nine tenths of the way.

divergence_note: The last two films were a blue-hour lab bench under the Chugach with a felt canary, a cobalt wall and a corridor planner (11-22), and an orbital night kitchen and walnut courtroom with a faced chat-bubble accordion and an auction tag (11-21). This film moves through an apricot-to-plum Interior dusk on the river ice: a cream map laid on the ice seen from above, a sepia 1925 depot and trail, a Nenana runway and hangar, a ground station, a test table by a cold window, a village at dusk and a night runway. Its motion is lateral (dogs, a train, a drone, a ribbon laid along a trail) instead of 11-22's rise, its hero pair is two glass tubes instead of a bird, and its machine is drawn plain with no face. Honest overlaps: a quote plate and a faceless named person with a boxed tag (house grammar), and a dusk exterior (11-22 ended at a dusk wall; here the light is apricot and plum on ice, never cyan or teal).

treatment.title: Two Runs Out of Nenana
treatment.summary: Two Runs Out of Nenana (Dramatist winner, grafted with the Comedian's string gag and the Explainer's sight bubble, restaged at Gate 0B). A cream map on the frozen Tanana at dusk: a sepia dog team inks a curving paw trail all the way to Nome, then a drone's shadow glances at an unlit village pin and closes ONE LOOP on NENANA. 1925 in sepia (diphtheria, train to Nenana, 20 mushers, 674 miles, a small airplane engine at 40 below). August 19th in summer green: the plain ULTRA rolls out at the Nenana runway, crosses the Tanana flats from above, a faceless pilot flies it from a screen, FLEW and STAYED split between a crate and a fridge, 8 HR 47 MIN. The signature: the ribbon lays itself along the trail and stops about nine tenths of the way, the lead dog sniffs the end, and it snaps back into A TEST LOOP. Small drones at 40 below. The Test by a cold window: Cahill lifts both clear tubes under her quote, steps away, the printer's tray stays empty (LAB RESULTS · NOT PUBLISHED), the empty crate turns to NOT TESTED FOR DOPING. The village, 82 percent off the road. A new strand reaches for the village and snags on a sight bubble (federal rules). A dashed radar, PLANNED, ghosts through the wing, a link line breaks, the arc tracks a dashed ghost airplane. Partners as plates over a dark village runway. The button: ribbon solid inside the bubble, dashed phosphor to the clinic.
treatment.judge_reasoning: D is the only pitch whose throughline object changes state at every act boundary, and its Test credits Cahill while separating small drones from the ULTRA and simulated blood from real blood. One map on the ice gives it a single fresh world for most of the film. The judge took the 621 against 674 gag from B and the sight bubble from C, and rewrote D's loop 1 because no source says why the drone flew a loop, so the film never suggests it came home because of FAA rules.

angle.thesis: In 1925 the serum for Nome left Nenana behind dogs because nobody knew how a small engine would take forty below; in 2026 a drone out of the same town flew a loop nearly as long as that whole trail with human blood aboard, and the next gate UAF names isn't the cold or the distance, it's a radar that would let it fly beyond its pilot's sight, so the win is real and the delivery still waits on permission.
angle.falsifiability: False if the flown samples, once anyone publishes the comparison (c7, c16), turn out degraded against the ones kept on the ground, which would put the cargo, not permission, back as the gate. False if TCC or Ryan Air start delivering medicine beyond line of sight with no detect-and-avoid radar fitted (c29, c30). False if the ULTRA itself can't fly in deep cold, since the forty below record is for small drones (c26).
supporting_facts: The flight happened. 1,000 km in a loop out of and back to Nenana, 8 hours 47 minutes, human blood samples aboard, flown remotely by UAF pilots (c1, c2, c3, c4, c13, c43). The agency's 2022 tests moved samples up to 20 km (c41).

The cold question of 1925 has an answer for small drones. Nobody knew how a small engine would handle forty below (c25). UAF has flown small drones at forty below and dropped a defibrillator, simulated blood and a rescue sled at 18 below (c26, c27, c28).

The next step UAF names is a radar. Detect-and-avoid is planned for both drones (c30), Cahill calls it a key step toward real-world medical delivery (c33), under rules that regulate against flying beyond the operator's sight (c29).

The need hasn't moved. 82 percent of communities are off the road system (c19), CMS says winter medicine delays of 5 to 14 days are common (c18), and TCC and Ryan Air are partnering with UAF on medical delivery operations (c34, c35).
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: 'The blood could survive' is Cahill's statement (c15). No lab results have been published (c16), the samples weren't tested for doping or medical conditions (c6), the January drop used simulated blood (c27), the loop landed where it started (c2), and the money is still building a framework first (c36, c37). Act 3 draws the two clear tubes side by side, a results printer whose tray stays empty, and the empty crate turned to NOT TESTED FOR DOPING, with the loop closing on Nenana instead of reaching a village.
angle.valence: celebratory, narrowed honestly. The analysts split (one celebratory, two curious or mixed). The synthesis credits the capability plainly because the record supports it (an 8 hour 47 minute flight with a ground control built in, cold work at forty below), and the counterpoint gets a full scene. It never says delivery is close, never says the blood was proven, never calls the flight autonomous.
angle.who_it_serves: Interior villages TCC serves (c35), rural patients waiting on medicine (c17, c18), and the 82 percent of communities off the road (c19).

second_movement.recontextualizing_fact: c43 against c22. The dogs carried the serum 674 miles from Nenana to Nome, an actual delivery. The drone flew about 621 miles, nearly the whole trail's length, and landed back in Nenana. The first read ('drone beats dogs') becomes 'the drone has the legs for the trip and hasn't been cleared to take it'.
second_movement.fair_case_against_scene: The two tubes, one flown and one kept on the ground, sit side by side by a cold window; a results printer lands and its tray stays empty (LAB RESULTS NOT PUBLISHED), and the empty crate turns to show NOT TESTED FOR DOPING (c7, c16, c6). The film survives it by narrowing: it claims the trip, not the result.

runner_up_angles.angle: Enthusiast: 'what's left is a radar and a rule, not whether the aircraft can do the job'
runner_up_angles.why_lost: overclaims the machine (forty below is small drones, the loop wasn't a delivery, no lab results)

runner_up_angles.angle: Skeptic: 'cold and range are no longer the constraint, permission is, and it hangs on a radar only planned'
runner_up_angles.why_lost: structure kept, but it rushed past the win and leaned on the News-Miner's 'critical step' framing as if permission hung on the radar alone

runner_up_angles.angle: Historian: 'the machine isn't what holds delivery back, and the geography hasn't moved'
runner_up_angles.why_lost: its second movement said the drone flew farther than the dogs; 1,000 km is about 621 miles, shorter than 674, corrected in the synthesis

angle.absence_checks: No lab results published: both validators read the UAF/GI release, DroneLife, KTUU and the News-Miner in full for laboratory figures; none report any. Stated as 'not published', never 'none exists'.

open_loop.what: Could it reach a village? Planted as the drone shadow glances at an UNLIT VILLAGE PIN and closes ONE LOOP on NENANA, carried as the ribbon lays along the trail and snaps back to A TEST LOOP, paid when the dashed DETECT AND AVOID RADAR · PLANNED pops up by the parked drone: UAF names the next step, a radar.

open_loop_2.what: Did the blood make it? Planted as STAYED's fridge door swings shut and the two tubes look at each other (one flew, one stayed, to compare), paid when the printer's tray between them stays empty: LAB RESULTS · NOT PUBLISHED.
